title: Elastic Plan Switching and Reserved Credit Allocation PRD
creator: Aria Patel
description: Enable customers to self-serve switch subscription plans mid-billing-period while ensuring predictable billing via reserved credit allocation, deterministic proration, and safe negative-balance handling. This feature targets customers who want to upgrade/downgrade plans without manual finance intervention, and platform teams that need clear, testable billing acceptance criteria.
background: Customers and sales teams report friction when moving between plan tiers mid-cycle: invoices and credit balances can be confusing, burst credits may be lost or double-counted, and engineering teams receive ad-hoc requests to manually adjust entitlements. Current behavior: plan changes create immediate entitlement delta but billing/proration logic is handled asynchronously in backend jobs, which can produce temporary inconsistencies in the Console and alerts from Trust & Safety when limits briefly exceed new plan caps.
goals: Support immediate, self-serve plan changes with deterministic credit reservation that ensures customers can consume promised burst credits immediately after switch.
Ensure invoice/proration math is auditable and reproducible (same input data -> same invoice delta).
Prevent transient SLO violations caused by delayed billing reconciliation (no temporary allowance beyond new plan limits unless explicitly part of a grace policy).
Provide end-to-end UX in Console and API including clear messaging, pre-change estimate, and post-change invoice link.
non_goals: Replace long-running enterprise billing reconciliation flows (those remain offline jobs for legal/regulatory reasons).
Support custom per-customer billing rules that deviate from the standard proration model (handled by account reps).
user_stories: As a developer on a mid-market account, I can upgrade from an S1 plan to S2 and immediately consume reserved burst credits on the new plan without waiting for overnight reconciliation.
As a finance admin, I can see a clear pre-change estimate showing prorated charges and remaining credit balances before confirming the switch.
As a platform engineer, I can rely on deterministic ledger events to build tests and alerts for billing anomalies.
As a customer success rep, I can rollback a plan change within 30 minutes if the customer reports unexpected behavior, with automatic credit reallocation and notification.
requirements: API: POST /v1/subscriptions/:id/switch with body {target_plan, effective_at: [immediate|period_end], preserve_credits: [true|false]} returns pre_change_estimate object and idempotent request token.
Console: plan switch UI shows pre-change estimate, clear notes on credit carryover rules, and explicit confirm button; must surface links to invoice and support contact on completion.

Credit reservation: when effective_at=immediate and preserve_credits=true, reserve the lesser of new_plan.burst_credits_remaining and old_plan.credit_balance, atomically decrementing old ledger and creating reserved bucket on the new plan.
Proration: charges and refunds are calculated using days-pro-rated on billing_cycle_start at UTC, with rounding rules described in acceptance criteria and documented in API reference.

Negative balances: allow transient negative balance up to -$100 or -X credits (configurable per-account), trigger automated email + Console banner and create a billing alert; do not automatically throttle API until grace window expires.
Auditability: emit ledger events for every atomic operation (credit_reserve, credit_release, proration_charge) with unique correlation_id and deterministic payload for replay in tests.
Telemetry: produce metrics and dashboards for PlanSwitch.Success, PlanSwitch.Failed, ReservedCredit.Amount, Proration.Delta, and NegativeBalance.IncidentRate.

Tests: include unit tests for proration math edge cases (leap year, DST boundary irrelevant since UTC), integration tests that simulate concurrent switches and request replay, and e2e billing acceptance tests that verify invoice generation on next billing run.
acceptance_criteria: API returns pre_change_estimate within 500ms for 99th percentile of requests under synthetic load (see perf budget).
For preserve_credits=true and immediate switch: reserved credit bucket is available for consumption within 2 seconds and ledger events are idempotent for retries up to 3 attempts.
Proration math matches finance reference spreadsheet for at least 20 randomized test vectors (provided in attachments) and rounding is documented and consistent across Console, API, and invoice PDF.

When switching from higher to lower tier with preserve_credits=false, any excess burst credits are released to a system-level soft-pool if the account has active grace policy; otherwise they are forfeited and a notice is recorded and shown to the user.

Negative balances: customers that hit configured negative threshold receive a Console banner and email within 5 minutes and the account remains unthrottled for the configured grace window; after grace window, automatic throttle behaviors apply and are reversible by finance action.

Rollbacks: performing a rollback within 30 minutes restores previous entitlements and ledger state and generates reversal events; automated tests cover rollback success, partial-failure, and manual remediation flows.
Observability: dashboards for the feature are live and show anomalies < 0.5% error rate in first-week rollout; alerts created for unknown ledger states or reconciliation mismatches > 1% of switches.
Docs: Console help text, API docs, and a short PRD summary are published before feature toggle is enabled in production.
Security: no plan switch operation exposes sensitive payment instrument data and audit logs include actor id, IP, and timestamp.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind account-level toggle. Phase 1: internal dogfood with sales/test accounts (2 days). Phase 2: opt-in beta for self-serve customers with usage < $10k/mo (2 weeks). Phase 3: gradual ramp to 100% with monitoring gates (1 week) and rollback plan. Finance retains manual override capability for first 30 days. Post-launch 2-week audit to reconcile ledger -> invoice matches for 100% of switches.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Race conditions between concurrent plan switches and consumption leading to double-credit usage. Mitigation: implement ledger-level compare-and-swap and optimistic locking with retries; include invariant-checking job that scans for mismatches.
Risk: Customer confusion around lost credits after downgrades. Mitigation: clear Console messages, pre-change estimate, and explicit checkbox to preserve credits (opt-in).

Risk: Unexpected invoice deltas generating refunds disputes. Mitigation: provide pre-change estimate and hold a 48-hour finance review window for high-value accounts; automated reconciliation tests pre-launch.
open_questions: 1) For preserve_credits=false downgrades, should we always move excess credits to a company-wide soft-pool or only when account has an active grace policy? (ops/finance trade-off)
2) Exact negative balance thresholds: propose default -$100 or -10,000 tokens equivalent. Should thresholds be per-account configurable at signup?
3) For immediate switches, is 2-second availability SLA for reserved credits acceptable to growth/solutions teams?
4) Do we need legal signoff for proration rounding rules in specific regions (EU VAT rules)?
